standard.title: Share with responsible media practice
standard.description: share media arts works in informal settings considering responsible media practice
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can share media arts works with audiences in informal settings and apply basic permission principles. They have not yet applied a full suite of responsible media practices (credits, formal permission workflows, audience and relationship considerations) when presenting.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students share media arts works in informal settings considering responsible media practice — including permission, credits, and audience/relationship considerations.

nodes.label: Responsible media practice in presentation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and apply at least two responsible media practices when preparing to share a work — including one permission/credit consideration and one audience consideration.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify and apply two responsible media practice requirements before sharing (e.g. create credits, obtain permission for photographs) — and explain why each is required.
nodes.typical_width: Apply responsible media practices across sharing contexts — creating credits for title sequences (font, colour, display time), seeking and acknowledging permission for photographs, considering audience and relationship when formatting a publication; apply media concepts of audience and relationships to layout decisions.
wider: Document a school excursion through photography — practising the full permission-to-publication workflow: seeking permission from class members, selecting and sequencing images, creating credits, and publishing to the school intranet
Develop and apply a class protocol for responsible sharing that addresses: individual permission, cultural material permission, credits, and platform-appropriate sharing
nodes.hinge_reason: Responsible media practice habits established here underpin all subsequent sharing and publication work — failure to establish the habit at Y3-4 creates compliance gaps in later years when stakes increase.

response_modes.reason: Responsible media practice is a procedural habit that requires repeated application across different contexts — not just conceptual understanding. Students need practice applying permission and credits workflows, not just knowing they exist.

success_criteria: Student can identify at least two responsible media practice requirements relevant to their sharing context
Student applies both requirements when sharing their work and can explain why each is needed

nodes.label: Sharing for audience and purpose
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can share a media arts work in an informal setting — applying audience and relationship considerations to presentation decisions.
nodes.minimum_width: Share one media arts work in an informal setting applying at least one media concept (audience or relationships) to at least one presentation decision (layout, format, timing, platform).
nodes.typical_width: Present media arts works in informal settings applying audience and relationship thinking; create title sequences with deliberate credits; format publications using appropriate text conventions; screen class-created moving image works; consider how the intended audience shapes presentation choices.
wider: Create a title sequence with credits for a class screening of moving image works — selecting fonts, colours and display timing deliberately, and reflecting on how these choices serve the audience experience

Format and lay out a front-page news story or print advertisement using available software — applying audience and relationship concepts to every layout decision and presenting the reasoning to the class

response_modes.reason: Audience and relationship thinking integrates responsible media practice with media language understanding — credits, layout and format choices are not just compliance but communicative decisions about how to treat an audience.

success_criteria: Student shares a media arts work in an informal setting applying at least one audience or relationship consideration
Student can explain at least one presentation decision (layout, format, credits, platform) in terms of its effect on the audience
